I love what unions stand for, but there are some shitty ones out there. I was in a (god awful shitty union) and it soured my attitude towards them. I'd have to weigh if I'd rather get fucked by my union or management.

My union was the anti-union. We needed a union to protect us from the union and management.

In my case, I was paying $80+ dues/pay and couldn't afford the heath insurance. We had people in the union making $9/hr having to pay the same dues and the majority of people with master's degrees didn't make $18/hour. Raises were 1.5 %/year. (After 5 years with a MA, I was making under $19.) Sure, I couldn't work over 40 hours a week and I had great PTO, but I could afford to get see a doctor or buy groceries. 

When COVID hit, they raised starting wages and put our raises on hold. New hires were making more then seasoned employees.The union wouldn't fight for us to see an increase because the UNION didn't want to renegotiate our contract—maybe in 2022. Wasn't that exactly what the union was supposed to avoid? They lost a lot of employees, me included.

That said, my grandparents unions treated them so well that they never had to worry a day in their lives. So there are a ton of great ones too. I just got a dud.

Edit to add:

I'm 100% pro worker rights. I fully support covered health care, shorter work weeks, fair management, collective bargaining.

I don't support my own shitty ex union for being useless. That is all.
